15 story files are `ready-for-dev` or `backlog`; none has an Implementation

That is the point. Sprint 1's retrospective action item was to run `/qa-plan`

## Finding 1 (BLOCKING for accuracy): GA-003 Deletes the Test File That Is Its Own Regression Bar

`tests/unit/gravity/gravity_component_test.gd` holds **26 cases** today. They are
the only characterization of the current gravity behaviour that exists anywhere.

GA-003's acceptance criteria delete `gravity`, `target_gravity`,
`baseline_ascent_mag`, `ascent_descent_ratio`, `set_gravity()` and
`update_gravity_lerp()` from `player_gravity_component.gd`. Verified against
`src/scripts/components/player_gravity_component.gd:16-72` — every one of those
members exists there now and is exercised by that test file.

So most of those 26 cases stop applying the moment GA-003 lands:

| Group | Cases | Fate under GA-003 / GA-002 |
|---|---|---|
| `test_apply_gravity_*` | 4 | **Survive unchanged.** These are the R4 "byte-identical magnitudes" evidence |
| `test_derived_dirs_*` | 4 | Migrate — `up_dir` / `right_dir` now read from the authority |
| `test_set_gravity_*` | 9 | Move to the authority; several are already duplicated in `gravity_authority_contract_test.gd` and should be deduped, not copied |
| `test_initialize_*` | 8 | 6 survive on the component; 2 reference the deleted `gravity` / `target_gravity` fields |
| `test_gravity_lerp_*` | 2 | **Deleted by GA-002** — `update_gravity_lerp()` ceases to exist |

**Why this is a QA problem and not a refactor detail.** The suite count will drop
below 178 during this sprint. A drop is indistinguishable from tests silently
disappearing unless it is accounted for case by case. And GA-003's AC4 says the
new magnitudes must be *"byte-identical to the pre-migration code for the same
inputs"* — if the pre-migration test is deleted in the same commit, that AC
becomes unverifiable and would be ticked on inference. That is precisely the
failure mode Sprint 1's retrospective named.

**Required, and gating on GA-003:**

1. The 4 `test_apply_gravity_*` cases survive **byte-identical in their
   assertions**. They may be re-pointed at the new call path; their expected
   values may not change. If a value must change, that is a retune, not a
   relocation, and GA-003's AC4 is violated.
2. `/story-done` on GA-002 and GA-003 records a **reconciliation line**: the
   suite count before, the count after, and the per-case disposition of every
   removed case — migrated to `<file>`, deduped against `<existing case>`, or
   deleted because its subject no longer exists.
3. No case is deleted without one of those three dispositions named. "It no
   longer compiles" is not a disposition.

## Finding 2 (BLOCKING for accuracy): Smoke Check 14 Asserts a Mechanism LS-006 Deletes

`tests/smoke/critical-paths.md` check 14 reads:

> 14. GameManager resets level state (plants watered, bucket, goal unlock) on restart

LS-006's acceptance criteria state that `GameManager.reset_level_state()` **no
longer exists and nothing calls it**, that `GameManager` holds only
`player_lives`, and that `restart_level()` is `reload_current_scene()` and
nothing else. Restart becomes reconstruction — the state objects are rebuilt,
not cleared.

The check names the *mechanism*, so it goes wrong the moment the mechanism is
correctly removed. Two bad outcomes follow, and both have happened before in
this project:

- The check fails for the right reason and is read as a regression.
- Someone repairs the check by preserving `reset_level_state()` — which is
  exactly what LS-006 forbids and what ADR-0002 exists to prevent.

**Fix, applied by this plan**: rewrite check 14 to assert the *observable
behaviour* rather than the mechanism. The behaviour is identical before and
after LS-006, so the amended check is correct today and stays correct
afterwards. Check 15 is left alone — level transitions are out of this sprint's
scope.

**Regression surface from this sprint, for whoever runs `/smoke-check`:** checks
**6, 7, 8 and 11** all exercise the gravity path that GA-003, GA-004 and GA-005
rewire end to end. None of the four is automatable — they are feel and visual
observations. They are the reason a human smoke pass is required before QA
hand-off even though this sprint delivers no new player-facing feature.

## Finding 3: Two OPEN Engine Unknowns, and What Discharges Each

Both are named in `sprint-2.md`'s Risks table. Neither may be closed on ADR text.

### GA-006 — ADR-0001 Verification Required item 2

**The question**: does a default-space gravity write made in `_physics_process`
reach every `RigidBody2D` in *that same physics step*?

**Status**: OPEN against the 4.7.1 binary. The `AREA_PARAM_GRAVITY = 1` /
`AREA_PARAM_GRAVITY_VECTOR = 2` spellings were confirmed 2026-08-14, and
`World2D.space` being dual-registered as both space and area makes ADR-0001's
part-4 snippet the sanctioned pattern rather than a workaround. **The
same-frame reach is the part that is unconfirmed.**

**What evidence counts** — all four, or the fallback is taken:

1. A `RigidBody2D` adopts the new vector on the same physics frame the player
   does, asserted in `tests/integration/gravity/space_gravity_write_test.gd`.
2. The same assertion at a **modified physics tick rate** (e.g. `Physics 2D >
   Default Physics FPS` at 30, not only the default 60). A guarantee that holds
   only at 60 is a coincidence of the tick rate, not a phase guarantee. A
   one-frame lag is exactly the failure the ADR item names, and it is invisible
   to any test that settles first.
3. The **asleep-body case** is run and its result recorded. Space gravity alone
   is not expected to wake a sleeping body. That expected failure is what
   motivates GA-007 — **do not repair it inside GA-006.**
4. The observed result, the date, and the engine build are written into
   ADR-0001's Verification Required field, and the `TR-gravity-012` note in
   `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml` is updated.

**The named fallback**: a dirty flag consumed by the authority's
`_physics_process`, costing one frame of stale space gravity at load. Choosing
it is a real engineering decision with a stated cost, not a workaround. If the
probe comes back negative, record the negative result and take the fallback
deliberately. Do not quietly widen the test until it passes.

**`/story-done` must not close GA-006 while ADR-0001's Verification field still
reads "Item 2 remains".**

### LV-006 — the headless `Area2D` extent read

**The question**: can an `Area2D`'s extent be read from a `CollisionShape2D` on a
node that was instantiated by `PackedScene.instantiate()` but **never added to a
tree**?

**Status**: OPEN. ADR-0003's E1 covers `@export` values and node transforms
being populated without a `SceneTree`, which is why the sibling rules are
CI-testable. Shape resources are `@export`-adjacent sub-resources and *should*
follow the same mechanism — but this specific read is **not covered by E1–E3**
and has not been verified.

**What evidence counts**: a probe against the 4.7.1 binary, run before any
`V-BOUNDS` assertion depends on it, recorded alongside
`production/qa/evidence/editor-facts-probe-2026-08-25.md`.

**If it does not hold headlessly**: report it as a finding against LV-006.
**Do not** substitute a hardcoded rect, and **do not** gate the rule behind
`OS.is_debug_build()` — the control manifest forbids the latter outright and
ADR-0003 Validation Criterion 3 covers both `level_validation.gd` and its call
site.

**Sequencing note**: LV-006 is Should Have and sits at the end of a strict chain
(GA-007 → PP-001 → LV-005 → LV-006). If the sprint cuts at the declared cut
line, this unknown stays open into Sprint 3. That is acceptable; leaving it
*undeclared* is not.

## Automated Tests Required

### GA-002 — Direction easing and the exported rate — Logic

**Test file**: `tests/unit/gravity/gravity_authority_easing_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- A 90-degree change settles within 100 ms and the angle is **monotonic
  throughout** — no overshoot, no reversal. Sample every frame, not only the
  endpoints; a mid-ease reversal is invisible to an endpoint-only assertion.
- The ease snaps to `target_gravity` once the remaining angle falls below
  `DIRECTION_SETTLE_EPSILON` (2.5 degrees, `0.0436332` rad).
- **R3 — strength snaps.** `ascent_magnitude()` and `descent_magnitude()` reach
  their new values on the *same* call to `set_gravity()`, before any ease frame
  runs.
- The ease runs in `_physics_process(delta)`, never `_process(delta)`.
- A smaller `direction_ease_rate` produces a measurably slower rotation — this
  is what proves the export is read rather than shadowed by a literal.
- No literal `32.0` appears in `gravity_authority.gd` outside the export default
  (TR-gravity-011). Assert by source grep, as the tuning suite does.
- No `move_toward` on `gravity.length()` survives anywhere on the authority.
- Once `gravity == target_gravity`, `_physics_process` returns without
  recomputing the angle or re-emitting.
- `gravity_changed` fires **once per `set_gravity()` / `reset_to()` call**, not
  once per ease frame. Count emissions across a full ease.

**Assert the margin, not only the pass** *(retro action item 4)*:
The margin is already computed in the story and must be asserted, not
re-derived. Settle occurs at step 5 = **83.3 ms** against GDD AC5's **100 ms**,
leaving **16.7 ms of headroom**; the 2.5-degree threshold clears the
1.9919-degree retained residual by **+0.51 degrees**. Sprint 1 shipped two
zero-margin thresholds that read as correct and would have failed on the first
legitimate change. Write both margins into the assertions so a future rate
change that erodes them fails loudly.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A 180-degree change — the `lerp_angle` shortest-arc path is ambiguous at
  exactly pi. Assert which way it goes and that it stays monotonic.
- A change requested *mid-ease*, before the previous one settles.
- A zero-length direction and a multiplier <= 0 — rejected, gravity unchanged.
- A change whose remaining angle is **already** below the settle epsilon.

**Estimated**: ~28 assertions.

### GA-003 — Player gravity component becomes a consumer — Integration

**Test file**: `tests/integration/gravity/player_gravity_consumer_test.gd`

**Read Finding 1 before writing a line of this.** The 4 `test_apply_gravity_*`
cases in `tests/unit/gravity/gravity_component_test.gd` are this story's
regression bar and their expected values may not change.

**What to test**:
- `player_gravity_component.gd` declares none of `gravity`, `target_gravity`,
  `baseline_ascent_mag`, `ascent_descent_ratio`, `set_gravity()`,
  `update_gravity_lerp()`. Assert by source grep — `var gravity` returning
  nothing is the `private_gravity_copy` forbidden-pattern check.
- `Player.set_gravity()` and the `target_gravity` proxy are gone, and **no call
  site remains anywhere in `src/`**. Grep the whole tree, not just `player.gd`.
- `Player._ready()` calls `GravityAuthority.initialize(baseline_ascent_mag,
  ascent_descent_ratio)` with the values derived in
  `PlayerGravityComponent.initialize(max_speed)`.
- **R4 — byte-identical relocation.** `apply_gravity()` produces the same
  magnitudes as the pre-migration code for the same inputs.
- **R5 — `jump_velocity` is derived once** in `initialize()` and never written
  again, including across every `gravity_changed` broadcast. Fire several
  broadcasts and assert it has not moved.
- **R1** — `up_dir` and `right_dir` are read from `GravityAuthority`, not
  derived locally.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Gravity angles 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees — GDD AC10 is the regression bar.
- A broadcast arriving **before** `initialize()` has run.
- Ascent versus descent at the same angle, to prove the asymmetry survived.

**Estimated**: ~35 assertions.

### GA-004 — Zones report to the authority — Integration

**Test file**: `tests/integration/gravity/gravity_zone_wiring_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- `main.gd` connects no zone to `player.set_gravity`. Zones reach
  `GravityAuthority.set_gravity()` and nothing else.
- `main.gd` connects `_rotate_camera_to_gravity` to
  `GravityAuthority.gravity_changed`, not to each zone's own signal.
- `gravity_zone.tscn` declares neither `gravity_space_override` nor `gravity` on
  its `Area2D` root, and **no other `Area2D` in the project does either**. Scan
  every `.tscn`, not just this one.
- **R7 / AC7** — a zone authored with a zero-length direction or a multiplier
  <= 0 is rejected **at the authority**, leaving gravity unchanged. Assert the
  zone itself performs no validation of its own.
- **R2 / AC6** — the player leaving a zone retains that zone's gravity
  indefinitely. Assert `GravityZone` has **no exit handler**.
- **R2** — entering a zone changes gravity globally, not for the entering body
  only.
- `zone_gravity_direction`, `zone_gravity_multiplier` and
  `get_zone_gravity_direction()` survive; `zone_priority` stays exported and
  unread.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Two overlapping zones, entered in each order.
- Re-entering the zone the player is already in.
- A zone whose direction is near-zero but not exactly zero.

**Estimated**: ~26 assertions.

### GA-005 — Level default gravity and reset on load — Integration

**Test file**: `tests/integration/gravity/level_default_gravity_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- `LevelRoot` exports `default_gravity_direction: Vector2` and
  `default_gravity_multiplier: float`.
- `LevelRoot._ready()` calls `GravityAuthority.reset_to(...)` at **init step
  3c** — after `validate()` (3a) and state seeding (3b), before zone and prop
  wiring (3d). Assert the ordering, do not assume it.
- **All 8 existing level scenes declare both exports**, with values matching the
  gravity each level currently starts in. This is the one story in the sprint
  that touches `level_01.tscn` … `level_08.tscn`.
- Restart via `reload_current_scene()` restores the declared default regardless
  of the gravity active at the moment of death.
- First load and restart go through the **same code path** — assert there is no
  first-load branch.
- No `reset()` method is added anywhere, and `GameManager.reset_level_state()`
  is not reintroduced.
- `reset_to()` runs after `Player._ready()` has called `initialize()`, so the
  authority's refusal guard never fires on a correctly wired level.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A level scene missing one or both exports — should surface via `V-GRAV-EXPORT`.
- Death while inside a zone whose gravity differs from the level default.
- A level whose authored default is not straight down.

**Note on scope overlap with QQ-03**: this story adds `default_gravity_*` to all
8 levels. It does **not** migrate them to the multi-bucket / computed-`O_level`
model — that is the unowned gap the 2026-08-25 gate ranked as concern 1. Adding
these exports must not be recorded as having closed QQ-03.

**Estimated**: ~24 assertions.

### GA-006 — Default-space gravity write — Integration

**Test file**: `tests/integration/gravity/space_gravity_write_test.gd`

**Read Finding 3 first.** This story discharges an OPEN ADR verification item
and cannot be closed on ADR text.

**What to test**:
- Both `AREA_PARAM_GRAVITY_VECTOR` (normalized direction) and
  `AREA_PARAM_GRAVITY` (magnitude) are written to the default 2D space obtained
  via `get_viewport().find_world_2d().space`.
- The magnitude is `descent_magnitude() * Tuning.PROP.prop_gravity_scale`,
  reached through the `Tuning` const holder — **never** a `.tres` path literal
  (V6).
- The write happens in `_physics_process`, never `_process`.
- The write repeats on **every** physics frame while `gravity != target_gravity`
  (`physics-props.md` R3) — props tip and slide *through* the rotation rather
  than snapping at its end.
- **The write stops once the ease settles.** Steady-state per-frame cost is
  zero. An implementation that writes unconditionally every frame looks correct
  and violates the `prop_gravity` guardrail — assert the call count in steady
  state is exactly 0.
- **R4 — prop gravity is symmetric**: the same magnitude applies rising or
  falling. This must fall out of using space gravity, not from added code.
- **AC12 — same-frame adoption**, at 60 FPS and again at a modified physics tick
  rate.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A body **asleep** at the moment of the change — record the result; the
  expected non-wake motivates GA-007 and must not be repaired here.
- No `RigidBody2D` present at all.
- A gravity change requested during an unsettled ease.

**Estimated**: ~30 assertions.

### GA-007 — Prop registry and the force-wake pass — Logic

**Test file**: `tests/unit/gravity/prop_wake_registry_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- `register_prop()` and `unregister_prop()` are implemented (signatures were
  declared in story 001).
- **AC3** — every registered prop is woken on **every** physics frame the vector
  is changing, not only the frame the zone fires.
- The wake call is `prop.sleeping = false`. Assert `apply_impulse()` and
  `apply_force()` appear **nowhere** in the wake path.
- The pass is guarded with `is_instance_valid()` on every entry, regardless of
  `unregister_prop()` being called correctly.
- Registering the same prop twice produces one entry, not two.
- `unregister_prop()` removes the prop and the wake loop stops touching it.
- **The pass does not run once the ease has settled** — steady-state cost zero.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A prop with `can_sleep = false` — a harmless no-op, not an error.
- A freed prop still in the registry. **Note**: in GDScript 4.7.1, `== null` is
  **true** for a freed object and `as` errors — use `is_instance_valid()`, and
  do not write the null check that looks equivalent.
- An empty registry.
- **The budget boundary**: the registry holds at most
  `props_per_level_budget` (40) entries in a correctly-authored level, and the
  pass stays inside the 16.6 ms frame at that count. Assert **at** 40, not
  below it — and record the measured margin under 16.6 ms rather than only that
  it passed *(retro action item 4)*.

**Estimated**: ~28 assertions.

### LS-001 — `LevelState` object — Logic

**Test file**: `tests/unit/level_state/level_state_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- **AC6** — `goal_unlocked` becomes true exactly when `buckets_consumed`
  reaches `buckets_total`, and never before.
- **AC8, lifetime half** — the type has no `reset()` and no way to clear state
  in place. Assert by reflection over the method list, not by reading the
  source.
- `buckets_consumed` never decreases and never exceeds `buckets_total`.
- `buckets_total` is immutable after construction.
- Assignment to `buckets_total`, `buckets_consumed`, `goal_unlocked` or
  `level_complete` from outside the class **raises a runtime error** rather than
  succeeding silently. Assert the error, not merely that the value is unchanged.
- `carrying_bucket` is genuinely read-write — the one field that is not
  getter-only.
- `bucket_consumed(consumed, total)` and `goal_unlocked_changed(unlocked)` are
  emitted, and `goal_unlocked_changed` fires **once, on the transition only**.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- `buckets_total` of 0 and of 1.
- Consuming one bucket past the total.
- Consuming the final bucket twice.

### LS-002 — `OxygenState` object — Logic

**Test file**: `tests/unit/level_state/oxygen_state_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- **AC3** — no game action increases `remaining`. No setter, no refill, no
  `reset()`.
- **AC6, arithmetic half** — with `drain_rate` 1.0, draining a fixed timestep
  repeatedly for `capacity` seconds of accumulated delta brings `remaining` to
  **exactly zero within float tolerance**. State the tolerance explicitly; do
  not use a bare `==`. The wall-clock half belongs to the `oxygen-drain` epic.
- **AC7** — construction with `capacity <= 0` is refused.
- **AC4 / AC5, lifetime half** — no refill and no in-place reset exist, so
  "restart refills" and "oxygen does not carry between levels" hold by object
  lifetime.
- **AC10, logic half** — `threshold_changed` fires at the `OxygenTuning` bands
  (0.50 / 0.25 / 0.10) and **never re-fires for a band already entered**.
- `depleted` emits **exactly once**.
- `drain()` is unconditional — it contains no state checks, so no caller can
  construct a safe state (R2, AC1).
- External assignment to `capacity`, `remaining`, `fraction` or `band` raises a
  runtime error.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A drain step that lands **exactly** on a band boundary — 0.50, 0.25, 0.10.
  Assert which side the boundary belongs to and document the choice.
- A single `drain()` large enough to cross two bands at once. Both
  `threshold_changed` emissions, or one? Decide and assert.
- Draining past zero.
- `drain(0.0)` and a negative delta.

### LS-003 — Frame priority contract — Logic

**Test file**: `tests/unit/level_state/frame_priority_test.gd`

**This is a 1-hour story whose whole point is an ordering assertion, and
order-dependent tests are exactly the ones that pass for the wrong reason.**
Before writing it, state what a real failure looks like: a test that would still
be green if all three priorities were set to the same value is not testing
anything. Include one case that **deliberately mis-orders** the constants in a
local fixture and confirms the assertion goes red.

**What to test**:
- A const-only script declares `-100` for `GravityAuthority`, `0` for `Player`,
  `+100` for `OxygenDrain`.
- The script holds constants and nothing else — no methods, no variables, no
  signals, no `_ready` — and is **not** an autoload. Assert by reflection.
- The constants are reachable from an autoload existing before any level scene
  loads, **and** from a level-scene node, by the same mechanism.
- **No `.tscn` file sets `process_physics_priority` in the inspector.** Scan
  every scene file.
- **No script in `src/` uses `process_priority`** to order a `_physics_process`
  callback. This is the substantive check — `process_priority` and
  `process_physics_priority` are different properties and using the former to
  order physics is the bug this contract prevents.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- The relative ordering, not the literal values: authority < player < drain must
  hold as an inequality, so a future renumbering that preserves order still
  passes and one that inverts it fails.

### LS-004 — `LevelRoot` construction and injection — Integration

**Test file**: `tests/integration/level_state/level_root_injection_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- `LevelRoot._ready()` constructs `LevelState(buckets_total)` and
  `OxygenState(capacity, tuning)` from its own `@export`s **at step (a), before
  any binding**.
- `buckets_total` is seeded from `LevelValidation.count_buckets()` — the same
  primitive `validate()` uses — and **not** from a group count.
- `Player` / `PlayerWateringComponent`, `Goal`, `HUD` and `OxygenDrain` each
  receive their state through a `bind(...)` call from `LevelRoot._ready()`.
- **Every bound consumer refuses to operate before `bind()` has run, with
  `push_error()` AND an early `return`.** Both halves — a `push_error` that
  falls through still runs the body. Assert the early return separately.
- Each `Plant.pour_completed` is connected by `LevelRoot` to
  `LevelState.consume_bucket()`; `Plant` receives no state object at all.
- `OxygenDrain` is a child of `LevelRoot`, not of `Player`.
- **Every bound consumer is a descendant of `LevelRoot`** — the A2-03 invariant.
- The group-based plant discovery in `main.gd` is replaced by a recursive type
  scan.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A consumer method called before `bind()`.
- `bind()` called twice on the same consumer.
- A level with zero plants and one with zero buckets.
- A consumer that is **not** a descendant of `LevelRoot` — must be caught.

### LS-005 — `level_complete` latch — Logic

**Test file**: `tests/unit/level_state/level_complete_latch_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- `mark_complete()` sets `_level_complete` true and is the **only** path that
  writes it.
- **Once true, still true on every subsequent frame of that level instance** —
  no method, property or path sets it back to false. Enumerate the public
  surface by reflection and assert none of it can clear the latch.
- `LevelRoot._on_player_reached_goal()` is the only caller.
- The two existing `player_reached_goal` connections in `main.gd` are replaced
  by **one ordered handler that sets the latch before anything else it does**.
  Assert the ordering — this is the ADR-0005 guard.
- `Goal` emits `player_reached_goal` and writes no level state.
- Calling `mark_complete()` twice is harmless and does not re-emit.

**Explicitly NOT closed by this story — do not tick these anywhere**:
`watering-system.md` **AC13** (final pour on the depletion frame yields death)
and `suit-oxygen.md` **AC8** (airlock entry on the depletion frame completes the
level) both require `OxygenDrain` and close in the `oxygen-drain` epic, against
the latch this story provides.

### LS-006 — Restart is reconstruction — Integration

**Test files**: `tests/integration/level_state/restart_reconstruction_test.gd`
**and** `tests/unit/gamemanager/gamemanager_test.gd` — the existing file must be
**updated**, not left alone. It currently exercises `reset_level_state()`, which
this story deletes. Reconcile its case count the same way Finding 1 requires for
GA-003.

**What to test**:
- **watering AC8** — after restart: carry state cleared, all buckets present,
  every plant reads `buckets_received == 0`.
- **oxygen AC4** — restart resets `oxygen_remaining` to `oxygen_capacity`.
- **oxygen AC5** — oxygen does not carry between levels.
- `GameManager.reset_level_state()` **no longer exists and nothing calls it**.
- `GameManager` holds only `player_lives`; `plants_total` and the other
  level-scoped fields are gone.
- `restart_level()` is `reload_current_scene()` and nothing else.
- **No `reset()` or `clear()` exists on `LevelState` or `OxygenState`** — assert
  by reflection, which also re-guards LS-001 AC8 and LS-002 AC4/AC5.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Restart triggered mid-pour.
- Restart with the goal already unlocked.
- Restart on the frame oxygen depletes.
- Two restarts in succession.

### PP-001 — `PropBody` RigidBody and registry — Logic

**Test file**: `tests/unit/physics/prop_body_test.gd`

**Scope guard**: only story 001 of `physics-props` is in this sprint.
`art-bible.md` §1.3 defers the epic's content to Vertical-Slice tier. **Do not
write test cases for stories 002–006.**

**What to test**:
- `src/scripts/props/prop_body.gd` declares
  `class_name PropBody extends RigidBody2D`.
- `_ready()` calls `GravityAuthority.register_prop(self)`; `_exit_tree()` calls
  `unregister_prop(self)`. Both present, **neither conditional**.
- `collision_layer` is `CollisionLayers.PROP`, `collision_mask` is
  `CollisionLayers.PROP_MASK`, written through the constants. **No integer
  literal `8` or `9`** in the script or the scene.
- `custom_integrator` is `false`, `gravity_scale` is `1.0`, and neither is
  exported or settable per instance.
- `mass`, `friction`, `bounce`, `linear_damp`, `angular_damp` remain authorable
  per scene instance — the script neither overrides nor pins any of them.
- `prop_body.tscn` exists with a `PropBody` root and a `CollisionShape2D` child
  carrying a **valid** shape.
- The script references no player, plant, bucket, airlock or hazard, and has no
  `body_entered` / `body_exited` guard of its own.
- `prop_body.gd` and the test file are **warning-clean** under headless gdUnit4.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Free the node and confirm `_exit_tree()` unregisters it.
- Instantiate without `GravityAuthority` initialized.

### LV-005 — Wire `validate()` into `LevelRoot._ready()` — Integration

**Test file**: `tests/integration/level/level_root_validation_order_test.gd`

**What to test**:
- `LevelRoot._ready()` calls `LevelValidation.validate(self)` as step **(a)**,
  **before** `LevelState` or `OxygenState` is constructed.
- `LevelRoot` iterates the returned array and calls `push_error()` on **each**
  finding — not the first, not a joined summary string. Assert the call count
  equals the finding count.
- **The level still starts after findings are reported.** Validation never halts
  or aborts `_ready()` (D3.6).
- `LevelState` is seeded from `LevelValidation.count_buckets(self)` at step (b),
  never from an independent count or an authored total (D3.5).
- **The full corrected sequence holds, in order**: (a) validate, (b) construct
  state, (c) bind consumers, (d) connect `Plant.pour_completed`, (e)
  `GravityAuthority.reset_to()`, (f) wire zones and register props. Assert the
  sequence as recorded order, not as six independent facts.
- **No `OS.is_debug_build()` guard** at the call site.
- `assert()` is not used to report any finding.
- `main.gd` and the test file are warning-clean.

**Documentation AC — gating, and easy to skip**: `architecture.md` must be
amended to swap steps (a) and (b) in the §Frame update path init block, with a
note that validation reads raw scene data (ADR-0003 Migration Plan step 1). The
published order is defective as written; leaving it is how the next reader
implements the bug again. `/story-done` must confirm the edit landed.

**Edge cases to cover**:
- A level with zero findings.
- A level with findings from several rules at once.
- A level that fails `V-BUCKET-SUM` — state construction must still proceed.

### LV-006 — `V-PROP-BUDGET` and `V-BOUNDS` — Logic

**Test file**: `tests/unit/level/level_validation_prop_rules_test.gd`

**Read Finding 3 first** — this story carries the headless `Area2D` extent
unknown.

**What to test**:
- The recursive scan from story 001 gains a `PropBody` match and a
  `count_props(level)` read consistent with `count_buckets()` — one definition
  of "a prop in this level".
- `V-PROP-BUDGET` fires when the count exceeds
  `Tuning.PROP.props_per_level_budget`, **naming both the count and the budget**
  in the message.
- The budget is read through `Tuning.PROP` only — no `.tres` path literal in
  `level_validation.gd` (V6).
- `V-BOUNDS` fires when `level_bounds` is unset or does not resolve to a live
  `Area2D`.
- `V-BOUNDS` fires **once per offending prop**, naming the prop.
- **The combined report-all-failures test from story 004 (AC-6) is extended to
  seven codes** — this is the case most likely to be forgotten, because it lives
  in a different file.
- `level_validation.gd` and the test file are warning-clean.

**Edge cases to cover — both are boundary decisions, not lookups**:
- **Exactly at budget is VALID.** The rule is `count <= budget`, not `<`. Assert
  at 40 and at 41.
- **A prop exactly on the bounds edge** — pick inclusive or exclusive, document
  the choice in the code, and assert it. Either is defensible; an undocumented
  one is not.
- **`V-BOUNDS` and `V-WIRING` must not double-report an unset `level_bounds`.**
  Recommended split: `V-WIRING` reports the unset export, `V-BOUNDS` skips its
  per-prop pass when the export does not resolve — a per-prop extent check
  against nothing has no meaning. Assert whichever split is chosen.
- Zero props in the level.

**Documentation AC**: ADR-0003 Migration Plan step 8 closes here, and ADR-0006
Migration Plan step 6 is marked as the same action — **closed once, not twice**.

## Manual QA Checklist

This sprint delivers no new player-facing feature, so there is no new manual
surface. What it does deliver is a **complete rewiring of the gravity path and
of level state ownership underneath unchanged behaviour** — which is the highest
regression risk shape there is.

### GA-003 / GA-004 / GA-005 — gravity path regression
**Method**: Playtest · **Sign-off**: qa-lead · **Evidence**:
`production/qa/evidence/playtest-sprint-2-gravity-regression.md`

Run **after GA-005 lands**, not after each story — the three together are one
migration.

- [ ] Entering a gravity zone flips gravity and rotates the player correctly
      (smoke 6).
- [ ] The vertical gravity flip lever still toggles up/down gravity (smoke 7).
- [ ] The player walks on walls and ceilings in a flipped chamber without
      falling (smoke 8).
- [ ] Moving platforms still carry the player in every gravity orientation
      (smoke 11).
- [ ] Leaving a zone retains that zone's gravity — the player does **not** snap
      back (AC6).
- [ ] Death and restart return the level to its authored default gravity, from
      a death that happened inside a zone.
- [ ] Jump height feels unchanged at all four orientations.

**A human session is required.** Agent-driven playtests misjudge pacing and
timing-dependent outcomes, and "does the rotation feel the same as before" is
exactly that shape. This is a **regression** check, not a feel-tuning check —
the bar is "indistinguishable from before", which a human can judge and a test
cannot.

### LS-006 — restart behaviour
**Method**: Playtest, folded into the session above · **Sign-off**: qa-lead

- [ ] Player death restarts the level and resets watering and bucket state
      (smoke 13).
- [ ] After restart, every plant shows an empty progress meter.
- [ ] After restart, the oxygen meter reads full.
- [ ] Restarting twice in a row behaves identically to restarting once.

### BUG-0002 — `MovingPlatfornm` rename
**Method**: Smoke spot-check · **Sign-off**: lead-programmer

- [ ] `moving_platform.tscn` root is renamed and its four level instances update.
- [ ] Moving platforms still animate and still carry the player (smoke 11).
- [ ] Suite stays green.

**Sequencing**: land this **after** anything depending on CLR-003's playtest, so
the rename cannot invalidate that sign-off.

### The engine probes — GA-006 and LV-006
**Method**: Headless probe · **Sign-off**: godot-specialist · **Evidence**:
alongside `production/qa/evidence/editor-facts-probe-2026-08-25.md`

Neither is a manual QA item in the usual sense, but both are **observations that
must be recorded before the ACs depending on them may be ticked**. See Finding 3
for what evidence counts in each case.

**The windowed Godot editor segfaults on this machine.** Every check above is
either in-game or headless. Do not write an "open the editor" acceptance
criterion for any Sprint 2 story without a substitution plan.

## Definition of Done — This Sprint

A story is DONE when all of the following hold:

- [ ] Every acceptance criterion is verified — by a passing automated test, or
      by documented manual evidence with sign-off. **Never ticked on
      inference**: open the story file and read its Test Evidence status and
      Implementation Record
- [ ] A test file exists at the specified path for every Logic and Integration
      story — that is **all 15**
- [ ] The full suite passes with the documented command, **both** `-a` paths and
      `-c`. Baseline is 178/178 at sprint start
- [ ] **Suite-count reconciliation is recorded** for GA-002, GA-003 and LS-006,
      the three stories that delete existing test cases — count before, count
      after, and a per-case disposition *(Finding 1)*
- [ ] **Where a spec states a duration, tolerance or floor, the recorded margin
      is computed**, not just whether it passes *(retro action item 4)*
- [ ] `/smoke-check sprint` passes, run **after** LS-006 lands
- [ ] No regressions introduced
- [ ] Code reviewed
- [ ] Story file set to `Status: Complete` via `/story-done`
- [ ] **Actual effort recorded per story at `/story-done`** *(retro action item
      3 — Sprint 1's estimation accuracy came back NOT MEASURABLE because no
      story file, sprint row or commit recorded effort anywhere)*
- [ ] **Every new CI guard has one recorded live-fire run** — "configured" is
      not "observed" *(retro action item 2)*

### How the two new DoD clauses are actually checked

Restating a clause is not enforcing it. Each is checked as follows:

**"A CI guard needs one recorded live-fire run."**
Sprint 2 adds **no new CI guard** — the four that exist were all live-fired on
2026-08-25. So this clause has **no live subject this sprint**, and that is the
honest answer rather than a manufactured one. It becomes live again the moment
anyone adds a step to `.github/workflows/tests.yml`. The check at sprint close
is: `git diff` the workflow file across the sprint; if it gained a step, that
step needs an evidence entry in `production/qa/evidence/` before the owning
story closes.

**"Actual effort recorded per story."**
The check is mechanical: at sprint close, every row in `sprint-status.yaml` with
`status: done` must carry a non-empty `actual_days` field alongside its
`estimate_days`. The field does not exist in the schema today — **PROC-1 must
add it**, or the clause is unsatisfiable in exactly the way Sprint 1's QA-plan
Nice-to-Have was. This is a dependency of the DoD on a Nice-to-Have row, which
is the same trap Sprint 1 fell into; flagging it rather than repeating it.
